notes.title: #3 - Ballotoro is released. What's next?
notes.notes: [h3][b]🚨[/b][/h3][p]So[b] Ballotoro[/b] is a short, chaotic game about rolling a ball. It's out now.[/p][p]It was built in just one month, and while I don’t expect it to sell long-term, I’m genuinely happy to see people playing it.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3807080/Ballotoro"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Ballotoro taught me a lot about game development.[/p][p]It’s simple, messy, and fast — and that’s exactly what I feel "fun".[/p][p][/p][p]Before this, I was working on a much bigger project called [b]End Turn[/b].[/p][p]It had a unique idea, and I pushed "hard" trying to make something grand.[/p][p]But a year flew by, and I burned out. It stalled.[/p][p][/p][p]Now, after finishing Ballotoro, I finally feel like [i]maybe[/i] I could return to End Turn —[/p][p]But this time with a better foundation and a clearer mind[/p][p](Actually, I don't know what my brain is doing sometimes.)[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3][b]What’s next?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Not sure yet. But I’m moving forward.[/p][p]Thanks for trying out Ballotoro — even a short game means a lot when someone chooses to play it.[/p][p]Ha, ha… One day.[/p][p]--[/p][p]flatcat[/p]

notes.title: A pause for something new
notes.notes: [p]I'm going to keep this simple.[/p][p][/p][p]I’m officially halting development on this project. It’s not because I gave up — it’s because I found something that hits harder, flows better, and genuinely excites me to wake up and build: Ballotoro.[/p][p][/p][p]I’ve changed a lot as a game designer since I started this game. What I want to make now feels different — more focused, more me. Ballotoro is where all that momentum is going.[/p][p][/p][p]If you were here for this project, thank you. Every bit of feedback and support helped me figure out what matters. I’m not throwing any of it away — just rerouting the energy toward something I believe in more.[/p][p][/p][p]If you want to know more about Ballotoro,[/p][p]click [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3807080/Ballotoro/"]here[/url][/p][p][/p][p]-flatcat[/p]

notes.title: Ver 0.3.9 - Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Enemiy in this game is called Foe

- Foe may come in formation of 5
- Total health is determined by number of turns passed. Distributed fairly
- Player can select which foe is targeted for effects. Select again to deselect
- Wave ends when all foes destroyed
- Adjusted playflow
- Removed kill counter
- Fixed bugs

notes.title: DevLog #1 - Introduction
notes.notes:
[b]Devlog #1 – Progress Update[/b]
by FlatCat

Hello,
I’m FlatCat, a solo dev working on End Turn, an auto deckbuilding game. Still figuring things out — you know how it is.

I’ve always liked dungeon crawlers, but they’re often bloated. I also enjoy deckbuilders and survivor-likes — fast, back-to-back action. End Turn blends those into short, semi-idle sessions where you manage and tweak your deck.

Save/load and UI are done. The loop feels good. What’s missing is content: upgrades, passives, proper enemies. Right now, they’re just HP bars — but even so, it plays surprisingly well.

This started as a 3D real-time card battler with AI summons. It got out of hand. I scrapped it and refocused on the current version you are seeing.

Next step: first full playtest to see what breaks.

If that sounds interesting, wishlist the game. More updates coming.

– FlatCat
